Local Ollama versions of every workflow (no API key needed)
Ad performance monitoring with auto-pause templates
description:
n8n Marketing Flows is a library of 79 one-click import workflows for n8n that covers the standard marketing automation jobs: scheduling social posts, monitoring sentiment on forums, digesting AI news, managing ads, and generating images and video. Each template ships as a JSON file you import into n8n, connect your own API keys, change the example parameters, and activate. The templates are in Traditional Chinese with English documentation, and every one lists which credentials it needs before you import.

The AI parts are real but replaceable. Draft workflows call an LLM node for post copy and hashtags, and a local version of every flow swaps the LLM call for Ollama, so the generation and analysis parts run free on your own machine. Only the platform nodes, publishing to Meta, reading YouTube data, writing to Sheets, need paid API keys. The ad management templates include an auto-pause flow for underperforming Meta ads.

Setup assumes you already run n8n or can spin one up with a one-line Docker command. If you have never touched n8n, the templates still work but you will learn the interface first. The docs are Chinese-first, which narrows the audience, though the workflow files themselves are language-neutral.

The directory already has an n8n entry for the platform itself. This is a template pack on top of it, and the honest comparison is that you could build these flows yourself in a weekend. What you pay for is the structure and the verified credential mapping. It is the cheapest way to stand up a working marketing automation stack, and it fits n8n users who want proven flows without rebuilding them, especially teams running Ollama locally who want AI features with no per-call cost.

seo_description: n8n Marketing Flows — 79 free one-click n8n workflows for social, monitoring, ads, SEO. Open source. Compare AI features & integrations.

hands_on: The package is 79 importable n8n workflow JSON templates covering social posting, sentiment monitoring, news digests, ad management, and AI image/video generation, each with Chinese-language documentation, node flow, and the credentials required. The template table marks workflows as verified, and two variants exist per flow: a standard JSON (defaulting to Claude plus email) and a .local-ollama.json variant that runs against a local Ollama instance with no API keys, using Discord webhooks for monitoring alerts. Setup follows n8n convention: import the JSON, attach your own credentials, adjust example parameters, activate. Based on the repository documentation; we have not imported the templates into a production n8n instance.

The project states all workflows are independent implementations with original copy, inspired by common marketing-automation scenarios rather than ports of third-party templates, and the key-handling note is explicit: templates contain no keys, you bring your own, and platform ToS and rate limits are yours to respect. For Chinese-language marketing contexts (PTT sentiment monitoring, IG/Threads/FB hashtag drafting) it is unusually well targeted; for English-only stacks, some templates need adaptation.
deep_dive.verdict: The largest verified free template pack for n8n marketing automation, with a genuinely free local-Ollama path and honest credential handling. Recommended if you run n8n and want proven starting points, especially for Chinese-language social and monitoring workflows.

name: Warpdrive
tagline: Self-hosted open-source Pipedrive alternative for BD teams: pipelines and Gmail on your own box
price_notes: Free, MIT licensed, no per-seat billing. You pay only for the server you host it on.
description:
Warpdrive is a self-hosted CRM that reimplements Pipedrive's core business development loop: kanban pipelines, a deal workspace, contacts, and two-way Gmail. It runs on your own box under the MIT license, single-tenant, with no per-seat bill. The pitch targets small BD teams that want pipeline tracking without handing customer data to a vendor cloud, and the whole stack comes up with one docker compose command.

The AI angle needs an honest answer: there isn't one. No lead scoring model, no AI email drafting, nothing in the product that learns anything. The repo ships a CLAUDE.md and a PostHog MCP config, but those help developers work on the code, not users sell. Where Warpdrive earns its place is as a clean, actively maintained open-source CRM with a real email surface: open and click tracking, templates, merge fields, scheduled send, and Gmail threads linked to deals in both directions.

Pricing is the simple part. It costs nothing beyond the server you host it on. One compose file starts the app, a WebSocket server, a background worker, Postgres, MinIO, and Caddy handling TLS automatically. Set against Pipedrive's per-seat billing, the trade is plain: you swap a subscription for ops responsibility, and Google Workspace provides your SSO and Gmail OAuth.

This directory carries several open-source CRMs, and Warpdrive's niche is narrowness. Twenty is the bigger project with more objects and a larger community. EspoCRM and SuiteCRM cover more business processes. Warpdrive deliberately leaves products, invoicing, forecasting, and workflow automation out of scope, and its README says so in a comparison table. What you get is the Pipedrive-style pipeline plus Gmail, polished.

Skip it if you need marketing automation, forecasts, or mobile apps. The project calls those out of scope and means it. It is also one maintainer's work, in production for a single team, with 73 stars and 33 commits at review, so treat it as young software. For a solo founder or a small BD team that runs its own infrastructure and lives in Gmail, it is worth an afternoon to try.

name: SEO Skill Bench
tagline: Open benchmark that scores Claude Code SEO skills against fixture sites with planted defects
price_notes: Free, MIT licensed. Runs cost LLM API tokens only: leaderboard runs cost $1.70 to $4.46 each.
ai_features: Headless execution of Claude Code SEO skills
Blind judging panel for subjective calls
Token footprint and per-run cost measurement
description:
SEO Skill Bench answers the question every Claude Code SEO skill README can't: does the thing actually work once installed? It is an open benchmark that runs SEO skills for Claude Code and other coding agents against fixture websites with deliberately planted defects, then scores what they find. If you are choosing an SEO skill for your agent workflow, this is the closest thing to a published answer key.

The harness installs each entrant in a real headless Claude Code session (claude -p), not a simulation reconstructed from its README, and points it at the pivot-saas fixture site. Scoring follows a pre-registered 100-point rubric: 40 points for detecting planted defects, 25 for avoiding traps, meaning the skill never recommends fixing something that is already fine, 25 for blind-judged judgment calls, and 10 for execution. Scores are medians across runs. On the August 2026 board, SEOAgent led at 84.9 while the vanilla baseline with no skill scored 73.0. That spread tells you two things: skills can add real value, and some entrants score below doing nothing at all.

Setup needs Node and a Claude Code install. You run node harness/run.mjs with a skill id and fixture, then the score and judge scripts, and entrants register with a one-line entry in skills.json. The leaderboard also publishes what each skill costs, kept outside the composite on purpose: resident tokens the skill occupies in every system prompt, per-run cost, and median time. Runs on the board cost between $1.70 and $4.46 and took 405 to 779 seconds. Heavy skills like Corey Haines' Marketing Skills carry 8,770 resident tokens, which dilutes every other skill you have installed.

The big caveat is the maintainer's conflict of interest. SEOAgent, the company behind the benchmark, also ships the top-ranked entrant. The structural mitigations are real: published fixtures, deterministic answer keys, a frozen rubric, blind judging, and a harness anyone can re-run. Still, treat the leaderboard as a strong signal rather than gospel. The benchmark only measures technical on-site audit work against one fixture. It says nothing about content strategy, links, or your actual site. At about 50 stars the community is small, and the repo's value is its method more than its momentum.

Compared to picking a skill by GitHub stars or vibes, this is the most concrete public way to see detection rates and hallucination traps side by side. If you are building an agent-driven SEO workflow, run your candidate skill through this harness before you point it at a production site.

name: Budibase

description: Budibase is an open-source operations platform for building internal apps, automations and, since its 2.x releases, AI agents that act on operational data. You connect databases and APIs, design interfaces in a visual builder, and wire up multi-step automations; self-hosting is free under GPLv3, with paid cloud and business tiers for hosting, SSO and support. For marketing operations the practical builds are the internal systems generic SaaS covers badly: lead-routing consoles, campaign budget trackers, content approval queues and dashboards that join ad platform data with CRM records. Because it is self-hosted, lead data and consent records stay inside your own infrastructure, which matters for EU teams with GDPR obligations. The 2.x direction adds agents that work over those same data connections, positioned as model-agnostic. The honest trade-offs: data modeling is part of the job, the AI features are young, and marketing teams without any technical help will feel the friction that engineering teams don't. Against NocoBase, its closest peer in this directory, Budibase is faster to a working CRUD app but less deep on data-model-driven structure. At 28,000-plus GitHub stars with daily development it is one of the most active projects in this class. We have not run Budibase in production; this assessment is based on the documented architecture and public materials.

description: Appsmith is an open-source platform for building admin panels, internal dashboards and operational apps on top of databases and APIs you already run. Marketing operations teams reach for it when campaign data lives in five places and nobody wants to check five tabs: a single dashboard over the ad platforms' APIs, a lead-quality console next to the CRM, or a promotion approval panel wired to the warehouse. Queries are SQL or JS against your own connections, interfaces are drag-and-drop, and everything stays inside your infrastructure when self-hosted. description: NocoDB turns any SQL database into a smart, Airtable-style spreadsheet with forms, views, permissions and automations on top. It is free to self-host under a Sustainable Use License (fair-code: free to use, not free to resell as a service; the same class as n8n's license), with paid cloud and enterprise tiers. For marketing teams it is the most direct self-hosted answer to the spreadsheet sprawl that runs campaign ops: content calendars, influencer and partner trackers, budgets, launch checklists and lead lists become shared, permissioned bases over your own Postgres or MySQL, with forms feeding them and webhooks pushing events into the rest of the stack. Compared with Airtable, you give up polish and the native integrations catalog and gain data ownership, no per-seat cost and SQL access to everything. Compared with NocoBase or Budibase, it is much faster to value: if a structured table with views and forms covers the need, NocoDB is the shortest path, and it is the most popular project in this class at 64,000-plus GitHub stars. We have not run NocoDB in production; this assessment is based on the documented architecture and public materials.

description: Opteo is a Google Ads monitoring and improvement layer that sits on top of your existing account. The value proposition is time: instead of burying an account manager in performance data, Opteo surfaces the changes worth making and lets a human approve them. Feature groups cover keyword management, ad creative improvements, bid optimization, bad traffic exclusion, error detection, shopping ads, budget management, scorecards, alerts, and branded Google Ads reports, with Slack integration for team visibility.
